1	# fastText
2	
3	[fastText](https://fasttext.cc/) is a library for efficient learning of word representations and sentence classification.
4	
5	## What is fastText?
6	
7	fastText is a library for efficient text classification and representation learning. It can be used for:
8	
9	- **Word representation learning**: Learn vector representations of words (word embeddings)
10	- **Text classification**: Classify text documents into categories (e.g., spam detection, sentiment analysis)
11	- **Language identification**: Detect the language of text
12	
13	## Usage
14	
15	fastText provides a command-line tool with the following main commands:
16	
17	### Word Representation Learning
18	
19	Train word vectors using the skipgram model:
20	```bash
21	$ ./fasttext skipgram -input data.txt -output model
22	```
23	
24	Train word vectors using the cbow model:
25	```bash
26	$ ./fasttext cbow -input data.txt -output model
27	```
28	
29	### Getting Word Vectors
30	
31	Print word vectors for words in a file:
32	```bash
33	$ ./fasttext print-word-vectors model.bin < queries.txt
34	```
35	
36	Get word vectors for out-of-vocabulary words using subword information:
37	```bash
38	$ ./fasttext print-word-vectors model.bin
39	```
40	
41	### Text Classification
42	
43	Train a text classifier:
44	```bash
45	$ ./fasttext supervised -input train.txt -output model
46	```
47	
48	Test the classifier:
49	```bash
50	$ ./fasttext test model.bin test.txt
51	```
52	
53	Predict labels for new text:
54	```bash
55	$ ./fasttext predict model.bin test.txt
56	```
57	
58	Predict labels with probabilities:
59	```bash
60	$ ./fasttext predict-prob model.bin test.txt
61	```
62	
63	### Quantization
64	
65	Reduce model size with quantization:
66	```bash
67	$ ./fasttext quantize -output model
68	```
69	
70	This creates a `.ftz` file with reduced memory footprint while maintaining functionality.
71	
72	## Input Format
73	
74	### For Supervised Learning (Text Classification)
75	
76	Training data should be in a text file with one sample per line. Each line should contain labels prefixed with `__label__` followed by the text:
77	
78	```
79	__label__positive This movie was great!
80	__label__negative Terrible experience.
81	__label__neutral It was okay.
82	```
83	
84	### For Unsupervised Learning (Word Vectors)
85	
86	Training data should be a text file with one sentence per line:
87	
88	```
89	This is a sample sentence.
90	Here is another sentence for training.
91	Word vectors will be learned from this text.
92	```
93	
94	## Command-Line Options
95	
96	Common options include:
97	
98	**Dictionary options:**
99	- `-minCount`: Minimal number of word occurrences (default: 5 for word vectors, 1 for classification)
100	- `-wordNgrams`: Max length of word n-grams (default: 1)
101	- `-minn`: Min length of character n-gram (default: 0)
102	- `-maxn`: Max length of character n-gram (default: 0)
103	- `-bucket`: Number of buckets (default: 2000000)
104	
105	**Training options:**
106	- `-lr`: Learning rate (default: 0.1 for supervised, 0.05 for word vectors)
107	- `-dim`: Size of word vectors (default: 100)
108	- `-ws`: Size of context window (default: 5)
109	- `-epoch`: Number of epochs (default: 5 for supervised, 5 for word vectors)
110	- `-neg`: Number of negatives sampled (default: 5)
111	- `-loss`: Loss function - ns (negative sampling), hs (hierarchical softmax), or softmax (default: softmax for supervised, ns for word vectors)
112	- `-thread`: Number of threads (default: 12)
113	
114	**Quantization options:**
115	- `-cutoff`: Number of words and n-grams to retain (default: 0)
116	- `-retrain`: Whether to fine-tune embeddings if cutoff is applied (default: 0)
117	- `-qnorm`: Whether to quantize the norm separately (default: 0)
118	- `-qout`: Whether to quantize the classifier (default: 0)
119	- `-dsub`: Size of each sub-vector (default: 2)
120	
121	Run any command without arguments to see its full option list:
122	```bash
123	$ ./fasttext supervised
124	$ ./fasttext skipgram
125	$ ./fasttext cbow
126	```
127	
128	## Pre-trained Models
129	
130	fastText provides pre-trained models:
131	- Word vectors for 157 languages trained on Wikipedia and Common Crawl
132	- English word vectors
133	- Language identification models
134	- Various supervised task models
135	
136	Visit [https://fasttext.cc/](https://fasttext.cc/) for downloads and more information.
137	
138	## Output Files
139	
140	After training, fastText creates several files:
141	
142	- `model.bin`: Full model file (can be used for further training or getting word vectors)
143	- `model.vec`: Text file containing word vectors (one per line)
144	- `model.ftz`: Quantized model file (smaller, load-only)
145	
146	## Examples
147	
148	### Example 1: Train Word Vectors
149	
150	```bash
151	# Train skipgram model on text file
152	$ ./fasttext skipgram -input data.txt -output model -dim 300 -epoch 5
153	
154	# Get vectors for specific words
155	$ echo "king queen man woman" | ./fasttext print-word-vectors model.bin
156	```
157	
158	### Example 2: Text Classification
159	
160	```bash
161	# Train classifier on labeled data
162	$ ./fasttext supervised -input train.txt -output model -epoch 25 -lr 1.0
163	
164	# Test the model
165	$ ./fasttext test model.bin test.txt
166	
167	# Predict on new data
168	$ ./fasttext predict model.bin -
169	> This is a test sentence
170	```
171	
172	### Example 3: Quantization
173	
174	```bash
175	# Quantize a model to reduce size
176	$ ./fasttext quantize -input model.bin -output model
177	
178	# Use the quantized model (same as regular model)
179	$ ./fasttext test model.ftz test.txt
180	```
181

184	- Website: [https://fasttext.cc/](https://fasttext.cc/)
185	- Documentation: [https://fasttext.cc/docs/](https://fasttext.cc/docs/)
186	- Pre-trained models: [https://fasttext.cc/docs/en/pretrained-vectors.html](https://fasttext.cc/docs/en/pretrained-vectors.html)
187	- Language identification: [https://fasttext.cc/docs/en/language-identification.html](https://fasttext.cc/docs/en/language-identification.html)
188

190	
191	- Facebook group: https://www.facebook.com/groups/1174547215919768
192	- Google group: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/fasttext-library
193	
194	## References
195	
196	If you use fastText, please cite one of the following papers:
197	
198	**For word representations:**
199	- P. Bojanowski, E. Grave, A. Joulin, T. Mikolov, "Enriching Word Vectors with Subword Information"

202	**For text classification:**

207	- A. Joulin, E. Grave, P. Bojanowski, M. Douze, H. Jégou, T. Mikolov, "FastText.zip: Compressing text classification models"
